annotations.text:
Two concepts for the meditation timer, drawn in one shared system: dark espresso room, mango wood, warm sand, Cormorant Garamond numerals, Jost labels.
Each artboard has two tweak chips above it: duration re-labels the dial, progress scrubs the session to any moment.
A soft gong sounds at the start and at each quarter, and a longer, deeper one closes the sit. Tap the gong line under the title to hear the quarter gong; tap again for the closing gong (sound on). The bowl shows the three quarter levels as faint marks inside.

A · Wooden clock (as built)
The hand makes one full turn for the whole sit. Strong marks divide it; in the app you choose halves, thirds, quarters, fifths or eighths. No numerals. Mango wood, black steel hand.
New: an optional short koan, carved into the lower face. Use the koan tweak above the artboard to test different lengths.

B · Sand bowl
A thin stream of sand fills a turned mango-wood bowl. The sand level is the clock.
Strength: ambient and wordless, very restful.
Tradeoff: imprecise, you cannot easily judge minutes. The numeric readout below could be made optional.
